subject: Post-call: latency & capacity clarification for FastLedger inference
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@fastledger.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 7 Apr 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: latency & capacity clarification for FastLedger inference

Hi Samir — thanks again for taking the call earlier. Quick recap and a couple of follow-ups so we can recommend the right deployment path (Hosted API vs Dedicated capacity vs Private VPC).

Call highlights (my notes):
- Primary use: real-time risk scoring in the payment flow (sync call, single token generation per request mostly).
- Current latency target: p95 end-to-end inference latency goal ~120 ms or better; tail-latency visibility is important.
- Request profile: peak traffic expected ~400 concurrent requests (bursty e-commerce spikes), steady-state ~80–120 rps.
- Typical prompt size: ~90 tokens per request; occasional longer contexts up to 300 tokens for debug flows.
- Data sensitivity: PII in payloads; no current regulatory requirement for on-prem, but procurement may ask about network isolation.

Open clarifying questions for you so we can be prescriptive:
1) Confirm whether the 120 ms p95 target is for server-side inference only or end-to-end including network hops from the client to our API?
2) Do you have a sense of the distribution of short vs long requests (<=100 tokens vs >200 tokens) across peak windows?
3) Any strict requirement for data residency/isolated VPC that would force Private deployment, or is that a procurement preference if required later?

What we recommend given the above signals (preliminary):
- If you need predictable p95 under 120 ms at sustained peaks of ~400 concurrent requests, Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool) is likely the best fit — gives predictable tail latency and tuning options (fixed batch sizing, KV cache sizing, quant profiles).
- If you want fastest time-to-value and are willing to validate at lower scale first, Hosted API can be used for a short pilot; we would run a controlled soak and measure p95 at target QPS, but autoscaling behavior may add variability during high-consumption bursts.
- Private VPC/on‑prem is only recommended if procurement requires private networking or you need to manage keys locally — adds lead time and infrastructure coordination.

Attachments: I dropped a short capacity matrix and a Hosted vs Dedicated one‑pager (attached) that explain trade-offs and typical latency/throughput ranges.

Proposed next steps:
- You confirm the three clarifying items above (server-side vs end-to-end, token distribution, residency constraints).
- We propose a 2–4 week pilot on Dedicated (reserved) capacity: load test + tuning + baseline measurement. We can produce a draft SOW for review.

I'll loop in Karthik and Dev on the technical plan if you confirm the numbers.

Thanks — Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

---
Attachment stubs:
- post-call-capacity-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet)
- redwood-hosted-vs-dedicated-onepager.pdf (pdf)

From: Samir Patel <samir@fastledger.com>

Date: Wed, 7 Apr 2027 17:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: latency & capacity clarification for FastLedger inference

Eve — thanks for the clear recap. Quick answers below and a procurement contact.

1) The 120 ms p95 is for server-side inference only (we have CDN+network hops external to that). We measure client TTFB separately.
2) Token distribution: ~75% of requests are <=100 tokens, ~20% are 100–250 tokens, ~5% are the long debug cases (>250). During Black Friday-style spikes the proportion of short requests rises to ~85%.
3) Data residency: not required today. Procurement will want standard contract language and an option for VPC later, but not a blocker now.

Procurement contact: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@fastledger.com> — she handles SOWs and billing.

We prefer Dedicated if you can show that p95 is reliably under 120 ms at our expected load. Can you provide a ballpark pilot cost and expected ramp time (provisioning + tuning)?

-Samir
VP Product, FastLedger

Subject: Re: Post-call: latency & capacity clarification for FastLedger inference

Samir — great, thanks for the quick answers and for introducing Maria. Based on your clarifications, here's a practical recommendation and a concrete pilot plan.

Recommendation summary:
- Recommended path: Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool) for predictable p95 tail-latency at peak. Hosted API is an option for exploratory testing but won't provide the same determinism under bursty peaks.
- Key levers we'll use: fixed batch sizing to avoid tail amplification, small-quantization profile to reduce per-token runtime, and prefix caching for repeated prompt prefixes (reduces backend work).

Pilot outline (4-week example):
1) Week 0: SOW review & sign (1 week admin lead time).
2) Provisioning & baseline (provision Dedicated pool sized for estimated peak; smoke tests).
3) Controlled load test (scripted ramp to 400 concurrent short requests; measure p50/p95/p99 across token bands).
4) Tuning (adjust batch windows, kernel choices, quant profiles), then final verification and runbook handoff.

Ballpark pilot cost: estimate $28k–$40k for a 4‑week dedicated pilot covering reserved GPU time + engineering support and runbook. We'll firm numbers in the SOW (depends on instance family and committed hours).

Action items from us (I will own):
- Draft pilot SOW and share with Maria + Samir (attached draft).
- Create a perf runbook and load test script (link in attachments/Drive).
- Karthik and Dev will size GPU families based on token distribution and provide expected p95 curves by Monday.

If that looks reasonable, can we schedule an SOW review with Maria and your procurement team? I have availability Tue Apr 13 10:00–11:00 PT or Wed Apr 14 14:00–15:00 PT.

Thanks — Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
